messages:
Maria: getting CF Workers bug reports: SDK crashes with 'require is not defined' and Node builtin errors.
Kevin: Workers are ESM. Are users bundling CJS?
Maria: yes — repro shows `const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood');` -> 'require is not defined'.
Sam: short fix: ship an ESM entrypoint + conditional exports so bundlers pick a worker/browser build. Also produce a worker-specific bundle without node-only deps.
Olivia: CF has no process/fs/Buffer. Global fetch exists but differs. Avoid bundling node-fetch/stream polyfills for worker build.
Kevin: make fetch pluggable: `new RedwoodClient({ fetch: globalThis.fetch, apiKey: env.REDWOOD_KEY })` and default to node-fetch only when globalThis.fetch is absent.
Sam: package.json exports idea (conceptual): map import->dist/redwood.esm.mjs, require->dist/redwood.cjs.js, worker->dist/redwood.worker.mjs so bundlers choose correctly.
Olivia: types: our d.ts references NodeJS.ReadableStream. Publish a types/worker.d.ts with minimal ambient declarations to avoid TS conflicts for edge consumers.
Maria: sample quickstart for README (ESM worker):
``
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood';
export default { async fetch(req, env) { const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: env.REDWOOD_KEY, fetch: globalThis.fetch }); const r = await c.generate('hi'); return new Response(r.text); } }
```
Kevin: add CI smoke tests using miniflare to run basic SDK flows against the worker bundle to catch regressions.
Sam: I'll open a PR for exports/build and add examples/worker with esbuild config (format: 'esm', target: 'es2020', platform: 'browser').
Olivia: I'll prepare types/worker.d.ts and update README notes about common pitfalls (no top-level form-data/node-fetch, avoid dynamic require, don't assume Buffer).
deploy-bot: CI triggered for branch fix/edge-shim by sam — miniflare smoke job running.
Maria: thanks team — will draft support KB and ping when PRs land.
